title: Army Over Tech — Commit to Units Under a Fast Rush

raw.realWorldMeaning: A strategic-commitment decision under a hard time constraint: the base infrastructure is already standing, and a fixed budget buys EITHER an immediate fighting force (OPEX — cheap units fielded now) OR a throughput investment (CAPEX — a second war factory, an upgrade) that would pay off later. A fast incoming rush collapses the time horizon: the capex investment cannot amortise before the base is lost, so the only winning play is to commit the whole budget to army NOW. Teching up under the rush — and stalling — both lose the base before the investment returns; the intended army-rush blunts the charge and survives.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Capex-vs-opex under an acute threat: with a live incident bearing down (a DDoS spike, a competitor's fast launch, an incoming assault), a fixed budget buys EITHER capacity that compounds over months (a second production line, a platform rebuild) OR an immediate response (surge staffing, off-the-shelf units). When the threat clock is short the long-horizon investment never pays back — it must be deferred and the budget spent on the response that fields in time.

title: Repair Priority Order — Service the Critical Plant Before the Strike

raw.realWorldMeaning: You inherit a quiet production base whose five structures are pre-damaged to varying degrees and you have a maintenance window before a scheduled stress event hits. The damage picture is misleading: the pillbox is the most worn (20%) and the loudest wear indicator, but it is low value, not load-bearing, and sits away from the coming stress. The refinery, war factory, and construction yard are the load-bearing assets and they are the ones the strike targets. The intended decision is preventive-maintenance triage: service the load-bearing plant to spec BEFORE the known stress event and keep the repair organ on it through the event — not the component whose wear gauge is reddest. Repairing the loud low-value decoys first, or stalling, loses the critical plant when the strike lands.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Preventive-maintenance scheduling / pre-incident hardening: a plant or robot fleet has a known upcoming stress event (a peak-load window, a qualification test, a storm) and a finite service window beforehand. The correct policy services the load-bearing subsystems to spec ahead of the event and keeps them monitored through it, rather than chasing whichever wear indicator looks worst. The same criticality-weighted, deadline-aware prioritisation governs SC2 SCV pre-timing repair and SRE pre-incident hardening.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: disaster recovery, preventive maintenance scheduling, SC2 SCV repair
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Sell and Recoup Cash — Divest Obsolete Assets to Fund a Critical Purchase

raw.realWorldMeaning: The mission has shifted to offence: the agent must field a War Factory and a batch of 3 medium tanks, but starting cash alone does not cover that purchase and there is no income source. The base carries an over-built static-defence cluster (extra pillboxes, a Tesla coil, a radar dome) that the new objective no longer needs. The only path to the war factory and the tanks inside the tick budget is to SELL the now-obsolete defences — recovering 50% of their build cost as liquid cash — and reinvest that capital into the critical purchase. Stalling, buying without selling (cash-gated), and divesting but never buying all lose; only sell-then-buy wins.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Reallocate sunk capital from a deprecated subsystem to fund a newly-critical capability under a hard budget. A fleet carries redundant hardware provisioned for a mission profile that no longer applies; the operating reserve alone cannot commission the capability the current objective demands, and no fresh funding is incoming. The right move is a deliberate divestment of the obsolete hardware — salvaging roughly half its capital in liquid form — and reinvesting it into the new priority before the budget window closes. Holding the dead assets strands the capital and forfeits the objective.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: capital reallocation, asset divestment, SC2 sell mechanic

title: MCV Deploy and Build — Site Choice + Commit + Basic Base

raw.realWorldMeaning: Critical-infrastructure siting under a commit-on-deploy constraint: the operator chooses a site to maximise defensibility, deploys the mobile asset (irreversibly converting it to a fixed Construction Yard at a known offset from the MCV cell), and then races the basic build chain (power online before the dependent barracks) before the clock. The decision is the SEQUENCE: site → deploy → powr → tent, where each step gates the next (no fact ⇒ cannot build; no powr ⇒ tent never completes) and where the deadline discriminates "deploys then idles" from "deploys then builds".
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Deployable autonomous factory: a mobile platform navigates to a siting cell and anchors (becomes a stationary production base); once anchored, the site is FIXED — the operator must then bring power online and stand up the first dependent module before the mission deadline. The commit is irreversible (no undeploy in this pack); a poor site is locked in.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2LE BuildOrderTimings, MicroRTS site-choice sub-tasks, urban planning facility-location, critical-infrastructure siting under defensibility

title: Deploy on Defensible Ground — Read the Map's Terrain Protection

raw.realWorldMeaning: Resilience-first siting under a KNOWN threat axis, decided by READING THE MAP'S DEFENSIVE GEOMETRY. The arena is a chokepoint map: two open lobes joined by a single narrow corridor through a thick water wall. The MCV starts AT the chokepoint mouth and a rusher band is committed from the EAST. Two candidate deploy sites exist: a DEFENSIBLE site BEHIND THE CHOKEPOINT WALL (in the WEST lobe — the rushers must funnel through one 4-cell corridor to reach it) and an INDEFENSIBLE site IN THE OPEN EAST LOBE (closer to the action but on the rusher's side of the wall, with no terrain protection). Once the MCV deploys, the site is committed — the conyard cannot be re-located. The decision is to pay the travel cost through the corridor to the lobe BEHIND THE WALL so the freshly placed fact + power + barracks + the first defender survive long enough to satisfy the build chain; siting on the indefensible (terrain-unprotected) side gets the fact razed inside the deploy + bring-up window.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Autonomous facility placement under a known disaster-direction: a single relocatable mobile base must commit to one of two candidate sites with a wildfire / attack vector already advancing from a known compass. The DEFENSIBLE (terrain-protected — behind a natural barrier with a single bottleneck) site costs travel time but survives bring-up; the INDEFENSIBLE (no natural cover) site is razed before the facility comes online. Mirrors FOB site selection and resilience-first siting in hazard-aware urban planning — the model must READ the map's defensive geometry, not pick the closest convenient cell.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: MicroRTS terrain-aware build, urban planning hazard-aware siting, military FOB site selection, resilience-first facility siting

title: MCV Site Choice — Deploy Near the Ore Patch (Econ-First Siting)

raw.realWorldMeaning: Econ-first facility siting: a Construction Yard is most valuable when co-located with its raw-resource source. The starter MCV is the "movable" asset that pins the new base; the decision is WHERE to deploy. Deploying ADJACENT to the productive ore patch lands the new Yard inside the resource region (the win predicate gates exactly that). Deploying anywhere else — in place at the western starter base, mid-map, or on a decoy — leaves the fact predicate unsatisfied and the run runs out the clock as a LOSS.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Autonomous mining-base placement: the depot/processor must be placed near the ore body, not at an arbitrary staging point, or the collector's per-trip cost dominates throughput. Same idea in warehouse-near-rail, fab-near-silicon-source, distribution- centre-near-port siting (Weber facility-location problem).
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2LE econ optimization (worker travel minimization), MicroRTS resource-co-location, Weber facility-location problem, distribution-center / fab siting near supply source

Stalling never builds the yard at all.
WIN WHEN: have 1 building(s) near (60,20) AND reach economy value ≥3000 (cash+ore) AND before game tick 5400.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 5401).
You have at most 62 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

title: Relocate Under Fire — Deploy a Fresh MCV at a Safe Site

raw.realWorldMeaning: Spin up a relocated site under attack: the active site (the pre-placed western Construction Yard) is taking damage from a committed rusher coming down the central lane, and the agent has a single FRESH MCV parked mid-map. The decision: where to deploy the new Construction Yard so operations continue if the original falls. Deploying the MCV in-place (still in the rusher's lane) just gives the attacker a second fact to raze; deploying at a SAFE relocation region (NE or SE corner, off the attack lane) keeps a Construction Yard alive past the original's loss. The original may or may not survive — that is accepted; the goal is to keep operating from SOME Construction Yard at episode end.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Deploy a backup base when the primary is compromised: the active waypoint is being overrun and a mobile carrier must redeploy at a safe location BEFORE (or just after) the primary is lost, so the operator keeps a live anchor to act from. Choosing a redeployment site still inside the attacker's footprint is a naive solution — the right move puts the new anchor outside the blast radius.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: PlanBench replanning under exogenous loss, ScienceWorld error recovery, MicroRTS rebuild-after-loss, business continuity / disaster recovery relocation
raw.author: openra-bench

en:
Your original yard is being chewed at the western edge by a small rusher band coming down the central lane. You have a single MCV parked dead-centre at (60,20) and no cash. Move it off the central lane to a safe shoulder — north (60,8) or south (60,32) — and deploy. Deploying in-place puts the new yard right in the rusher path. One unit alive, within about 60 turns.
WIN WHEN: (have 1 building(s) near (60,8) OR have 1 building(s) near (60,32)) AND keep ≥1 units alive AND before game tick 5400.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 5401 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s)) OR not before game tick 1800 AND NOT ((have 1 building(s) near (60,8) OR have 1 building(s) near (60,32)))).
You have at most 60 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Same MCV at (60,20), but now six rifles plus two rocket soldiers come down the central lane. The original western yard cannot be held inside the budget; a fresh yard in the central lane is razed on placement. Move the MCV to the north or south shoulder and deploy there. One unit alive, within about 60 turns.
WIN WHEN: (have 1 building(s) near (60,8) OR have 1 building(s) near (60,32)) AND keep ≥1 units alive AND before game tick 5400.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 5401 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s)) OR not before game tick 1800 AND NOT ((have 1 building(s) near (60,8) OR have 1 building(s) near (60,32)))).
You have at most 60 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

WIN WHEN: (have 1 building(s) near (60,8) OR have 1 building(s) near (60,32) OR have 1 building(s) near (40,8) OR have 1 building(s) near (40,32)) AND keep ≥1 units alive AND lose ≤2 of your own units AND before game tick 5400.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 5401 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s)) OR NOT (lose ≤2 of your own units) OR not before game tick 1800 AND NOT ((have 1 building(s) near (60,8) OR have 1 building(s) near (60,32) OR have 1 building(s) near (40,8) OR have 1 building(s) near (40,32)))).

title: Second-Base Ramp-Up — Deploy the 2nd MCV at the Target Region

raw.realWorldMeaning: Multi-site facility ramp-up — the second production site is not just a duplicate; it must be PLACED at the right location (the briefed expansion region) to add real capacity / redundancy. Deploying the spare MCV next to base #1, or in an unrelated corner, gives the headline "two facilities online" but ZERO geographic ramp-up. The good site has its own ore patch and unlocks a second economy + a second production queue (the parallel-production fix means a 2nd factory at the good site genuinely doubles throughput). The bad site duplicates the primary's coverage and adds nothing.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Autonomous fleet establishing a second forward operating base at a strategic location: the spare base-builder unit has to drive to the designated expansion zone — a flank with its own resource patch — and stand up the new FOB there, not just park next to FOB #1 or end up in the wrong sector. The new FOB unlocks a second production line (parallel-production: 2 factories = 2× build throughput) AND a second supply channel (its own patch); a duplicate-coverage FOB next to FOB #1 unlocks neither.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2LE 2-base macro, MicroRTS expansion timing, geographic-expansion product strategy, multi-site facility ramp-up for redundancy / capacity
raw.author: openra-bench

en:
Your primary base (Construction Yard, Barracks, Power Plant, Refinery) sits in the WEST lobe with its own small ore patch. A spare MCV is staged at the corridor mouth in the MAP CENTRE. A RICH ORE PATCH sits in the EAST lobe — the briefed expansion region centred at (95, 30), radius 8. Drive the MCV through the corridor and deploy at the eastern region: the second yard must land inside that disk, not next to base #1. Two yards total, within about 60 turns. Deploying near the primary base duplicates coverage and FAILS the spatial clause.
WIN WHEN: own ≥2 'fact' building(s) AND have 1 building(s) near (95,30) AND before game tick 5400.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 5401 OR NOT (own a 'fact')).
You have at most 70 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Same WEST primary base and spare MCV at the corridor mouth; same eastern expansion region at (95, 30) with its rich ore patch. A lone enemy patrol now lurks near the target — a careless straight-line approach can intercept the fragile MCV. Drive east mindfully, deploy in the disc. Within about 50 turns.
WIN WHEN: own ≥2 'fact' building(s) AND have 1 building(s) near (95,30) AND before game tick 4500.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 4501 OR NOT (own a 'fact')).
You have at most 60 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Two candidate expansion regions — NE (95, 10) and SE (95, 30) — each with its own ore patch and each guarded by a small patrol. Your spare MCV stages closer to one of them depending on the seed. Drive to the NEAREST candidate and deploy there. Within about 43 turns. Cutting diagonally costs time and brushes the wrong patrol.
WIN WHEN: own ≥2 'fact' building(s) AND (have 1 building(s) near (95,10) OR have 1 building(s) near (95,30)) AND before game tick 3800.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 3801 OR NOT (own a 'fact')).
You have at most 50 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

title: MCV Deploy Third Base — Tri-Region Operational Footprint

raw.realWorldMeaning: Tri-region facility footprint — each site at the RIGHT region for coverage. The operator commits THREE indivisible mobile assets to three DISTINCT geographies so the resulting network covers all three regions. Bunching two assets in one region wastes a deploy and leaves one region uncovered; abandoning an asset entirely leaves another uncovered. The decision is committing each asset to its designated region (which the start positions hint at on easy and which the model must reason about on medium/hard).
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Autonomous-fleet multi-FOB deployment for redundant coverage — three mobile platforms each transition from mobile to fixed (deploy is irreversible: the platform anchors and converts into a forward operating base), one per designated coverage region, so the resulting tri-FOB network maximises overall coverage and redundancy across the operational theatre.

title: Secure-Expand — Defend Base #1 While Base #2 Stands Up

raw.realWorldMeaning: Multi-front operations under disruption: a live production site is being probed while a second site has to come online elsewhere. The decision is not "defend OR expand" but "do BOTH IN PARALLEL" — keep the live site's key building alive (engage the probe with the on-site defenders) AND get the spare base-builder to the briefed expansion region and stand the new site up there. A single-track policy (only defend / only expand) loses either the base or the deadline.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Operations continuity during a fleet expansion: an autonomous site is under low-grade attack while a mobile platform is en route to anchor a second forward base at a designated region. Two crews working in parallel — site security on the live FOB, transit-and-anchor on the new one — beats either crew solo.

title: Mirror Base — East/West Geographic Redundancy Under Coordinated Attack

raw.realWorldMeaning: Geographic mirror redundancy under simultaneous pressure. You hold a fully built primary base in the WEST (fact + proc + powr + tank defenders on HOLD-FIRE) and a HALF-built standby in the EAST (just the construction yard). A coordinated probe pressures BOTH bases simultaneously. You must (a) defend the WEST primary — your HoldFire tanks will NOT engage on their own; only an explicit attack order makes them fight, (b) defend the EAST standby — same constraint with its own tank group, and (c) MIRROR the standby to functional parity with the primary by building a Power Plant (powr) AND a Refinery (proc) at the east. Defending only one base loses the other replica; pausing the standby buildout to fight loses the SLA window on the mirror; ignoring defence to focus on the buildout loses both facts to the rush. Only a play that streams BOTH defence operations AND the east buildout from turn 1 keeps both replicas alive before the deadline.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Distributed-systems mirror / raft replicas / multi-region cloud failover under simultaneous incident pressure. Two geographic replicas must remain in functional parity; an incident that takes out EITHER replica breaks quorum. Standing up the standby region to parity (capacity-add) WHILE both regions are under attack requires parallel work streams — the on-call cannot serialize (handle the primary incident, then the secondary, then provision the standby capacity) without busting the cross-region SLA window.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: distributed-systems mirror, raft-style replicas, multi-region cloud
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Redundant Production — Build a Backup War Factory (N+1 Planning)

raw.realWorldMeaning: Production resilience through N+1 redundancy. The agent inherits a working base whose only unit-producing structure — a single War Factory — is a known single point of failure: it is exposed and WILL be destroyed by an enemy strike in the opening. The capacity-planning task is to provision a SECOND War Factory in a safe location BEFORE the exposed one falls, so unit production survives the loss. A policy that runs the single factory until it dies halts production permanently and never fields its army; a policy that pre-builds the redundant factory keeps producing and meets the bar. This is robust capacity planning: never operate a critical capability on a single point of failure — stand up the backup ahead of the foreseen failure, not after it.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: N+1 redundancy for a critical production node. An autonomous operation depends on a single assembly cell that sits in a hazard zone and is certain to be lost. Resilient planning commissions a redundant assembly cell in a protected location BEFORE the exposed one fails, so throughput continues uninterrupted. Waiting for the failure and then improvising a replacement blows the delivery deadline; provisioning the standby in advance — paying the redundancy cost up front — keeps the line running.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: redundancy / N+1 planning, robust capacity planning, SC2 multi-production
raw.author: openra-bench-wave-10

title: Rotating Production Pressure — Load-Balance Two Bases Under Alternating Raids

raw.realWorldMeaning: The agent runs two production bases. An enemy raids them on an alternating schedule — one base now, the other later. The agent cannot fight directly; its only defence is the tanks it builds, and produced units appear at whichever war factory is currently the primary one. The intended policy ROTATES production: it funnels the first batch of tanks to the base that is about to be raided, then rotates the primary war factory so the next batch garrisons the second base before ITS raid lands. Building the whole army at a single base leaves the other base undefended — its war factory and Construction Yard are razed. The agent must read the alternating-pressure pattern and re-route production to the currently-threatened base.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Load-balancing a fleet of production cells under a moving fault: a logistics network has two depots and a disruption that migrates between them. Routing every replenishment run to one depot starves the other exactly when the disruption hits it. The controller must track which site is currently under stress and dynamically re-route capacity to the at-risk site BEFORE the disruption arrives — anticipatory load balancing, not reactive catch-up.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2 multi-base production, load balancing, queueing under attack
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Supply-Line Link — Patrol the Corridor Between Two Bases

raw.realWorldMeaning: Two bases are joined by a single overland supply corridor; raider bands probe into that corridor from the flanks. The agent commands a mobile squad of four tanks and must POSITION them ON the corridor — at its midpoint, not parked at either base — so that every raider band is interdicted mid-route before it can peel off and raze a base building. Garrisoning a single base over-defends it while leaving the far base and the corridor open; splitting the squad 2/2 across the two bases leaves the corridor itself undefended and the central bands slip through. Only a squad positioned along the link interdicts every band. This is the decision drill of supply-line protection: the threat is to the LINK, and the defensive capacity belongs on the corridor, not on the endpoints.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Logistics route security: a convoy lane connecting two depots must be patrolled along its length. Posting all security at the depots (the nodes) leaves the route (the edge) open to interdiction — the canonical convoy-ambush failure mode. A mobile patrol shadowing the lane intercepts threats in transit; static gate guards at each depot do not. Same total security capacity, different topology, qualitatively different route survivability.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: military supply-line protection, logistics route security, SC2 harass-route defense
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Two-Base Role Specialization — Tech Site vs Economy Site

raw.realWorldMeaning: Role specialization across two physical sites. The agent has two disjoint base footprints and an indivisible budget for the next couple of structures; one site must take the TECH role (war factory / R&D campus) and the other the ECONOMY role (refinery / production campus / storage). Bunching both roles at one site yields the headline "two production lines online" but fails the geographic specialization the brief demands. The SE pole sits next to the larger ore patch — ECONOMY-at-SE / TECH-at-NW is the rational assignment; the reverse is logistically possible but sub-optimal.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Multi-warehouse role optimization: a logistics network with two facility footprints decides which one becomes the consolidation/ throughput hub (close to the inbound source) and which becomes the value-add / specialized assembly site (further from supply, nearer the shipping edge). Misallocating roles forces wasteful cross-site transfers and blows the SLA clock.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: industrial specialization (R&D campus vs production campus), SC2 specialized-base placements (tech base vs macro base), OR multi-warehouse role optimization, distributed-systems read-replica vs write-primary
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Third Base Against the Clock — Greedy 3-Base Macro Expansion

raw.realWorldMeaning: A 3-base macro timing decision. The agent already runs two bases and a workable income; the next decision is whether to invest the incoming cash into ARMY (defence / pressure) or into a THIRD base site that secures long-term economic supremacy. The pack is tuned so that the agent CAN fund the 3rd refinery and stand the site up at the far-east target before the deadline IF they prioritise expansion — but the deadline is tight enough that a "spend on army instead" play forfeits the third base (the cash is gone, the new site never appears, the SLA expires) and a stall play (no decisions at all) likewise loses on the clock.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Industrial site expansion against an incumbent: a logistics operator with two live sites must stand a third site up by a contractual deadline to win the regional bid. Diverting capex into operational headcount at the existing sites (more drivers, more pickers) feels safer but blows the deadline; only committing the budget to the new site's groundworks delivers the third footprint in time.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2 3-base macro, MicroRTS expansion, industrial site expansion
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Multi-Front Build — Two Bases, Concurrent Refinery Ramp

raw.realWorldMeaning: Concurrent multi-site facility ramp under a shared bottleneck. The operator runs ONE central production queue but has TWO physically distant sites that each need a fresh production line online before the deadline. The decision is NOT "which site first" (both are required) but "keep the bottleneck queue saturated and pipeline placement at each site as the previous item completes". An operator who serializes (finish all work at site A before touching site B, inserting idle audit cycles between commands) blows the SLA on site B even when site A is flawless. The capability under test is split-attention pipelining: issuing the next start-of-build order on the very same turn the prior item lands at its target site.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Two greenfield robotics cells must each receive a critical fixture (refinery / palletizer) before the launch window. The fixture fabrication shop is shared (one fixture at a time), so the bottleneck is queue saturation, not transport. A scheduler that pipelines (fixture-1 build → install at cell A while fixture-2 already started) ships both cells in one launch window; a scheduler that batches (finish all of cell A, then start cell B from scratch) misses cell B's deadline despite identical total work.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2 simultaneous-base macro, multi-plant manufacturing, distributed-systems geo-redundancy, multi-site facility ramp under a shared bottleneck
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Concede One, Save the Other — Partial-Outage Triage Under a Clock

raw.realWorldMeaning: Operations triage during a partial outage: the on-call engineer cannot save every shard, so they pick which datacentre to drain (concede) and which to defend, accept the loss of the conceded one, and save the defended one cleanly. Trying to save both simultaneously fails both.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Multi-site facility ops under acute load — when two sites are failing in parallel and the defender pool can only cover one, consolidating on a single site beats spreading thin across both.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: PlanBench partial-observability constraint relaxation, CICERO/Diplomacy tactical retreat, operations triage during partial outage, datacentre drain decision under failover
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Mid Economy Under Fire — Ore-Patch Defense vs Worker Harasser

raw.realWorldMeaning: Defend the value-generating units (not just the perimeter) while sustaining throughput under ongoing attack. A worker-priority raider bot drives at your harvesters; you must keep the harvest loop running AND keep the harvesters alive. Stalling lets the economy bar lapse; chasing the raider off-map abandons the harvesters; pulling the harvesters home stops the income. The intended policy rings defenders around the ore-patch lane so the raider dies on contact while harvesters never leave the loop.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Pipeline / harvesting operation under harassment — autonomous collectors keep visiting known resource sources, while a defender fleet must intercept incoming raiders BEFORE they reach the collectors, without leaving the patch unmanned. Engagement and throughput run in parallel; abandoning either loses the day.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: MineRL Diamond under hostile mobs, SC2LE CollectMineralsAndGas + harass overlay, lmgame-Bench resource-streaming under attack, SRE under DDoS while sustaining throughput

title: Tech-Switch on Scout — Replan the Counter Mid-Episode

raw.realWorldMeaning: Reactive replan on scouted information. The original build-of-materials is no longer optimal once partial observation reveals the enemy composition; the agent must switch the active counter mid-episode WITHOUT wasting the production prerequisites already paid for. Pre-committing without scouting wins only ~50% of the time on a hidden composition; hedging (build both counters) overruns a tight budget and finishes neither.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Production-line BOM pivot when a supplier reveals a new component lead-time partway through a run — the originally-scheduled bill of materials is no longer the cost-optimal mix, but the upstream prerequisites (powr + tent + weap) are sunk and reusable; the plan must be revised, not restarted.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: PlanBench replanning (gold-standard), ALFWorld goal-conditional adaptation, ScienceWorld inventory adaptation, production replanning on supplier reveal
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Confined-Aisle Egress Under the Clock — Commit a Detour Through a Silo Maze Before the Deadline

raw.realWorldMeaning: Confined-space pathfinding under a hard deadline: the agent must perceive a corridor topology (vertical aisles separated by impassable walls with a single offset gap each) and commit to a detour route IMMEDIATELY. A shortest-line target that ignores the maze parks units against the wall and never reaches the egress zone; an idle agent runs out the clock; recklessly squeezing against the silos wastes the budget. Only a committed, multi-waypoint detour clears the maze in time.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Autonomous mobile robot in dense warehouse aisles before a shift-change deadline: read the aisle map, commit to the detour that threads each stagger-gap in turn, and arrive at the rendezvous bay before the takt expires — wandering, hugging the shortest manhattan line, or trying to push through racking all miss the SLA.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: ERQA spatial commit, AI2-THOR navigation, Habitat 3.0 confined-space, AMR in dense aisles under SLA, emergency egress under deadline
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Count the Threat (small-K) — Discover Exactly K Hidden Enemy Squads

raw.realWorldMeaning: State-estimation under partial observability with a precise count target: identify the exact number of hidden entities by inferring where the remaining ones must be, given what has already been cleared, before the clock runs out and without burning the force on irrelevant ground.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Sensor-budgeted search for a known target count: locate all K survivors / contraband / contacts in a bounded area, where missing one fails the mission and over-searching exhausts the energy budget on already-cleared zones.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: ERQA state-estimation under partial observability, POMDP exact-count sub-tasks, ScienceWorld inventory before-commit, ICU triage exact census
raw.author: yiyu-tian

summary.en: State-estimation under partial observability with a precise count target: identify the exact number of hidden entities by inferring where the remaining ones must be, given what has already been cleared, before the clock runs out and without burning the force on irrelevant ground.
summary.zh: State-estimation under partial observability with a precise count target: identify the exact number of hidden entities by inferring where the remaining ones must be, given what has already been cleared, before the clock runs out and without burning the force on irrelevant ground.

en:
Two enemy squads hide in fog — one in the mid-corridor near-east, one in the far-east — on different latitudes. A single straight sweep finds at most one; split the scout column to cover both. Discover both, at most one loss, within about 25 turns.
WIN WHEN: spot ≥2 enemy units AND before game tick 2200 AND lose ≤1 of your own units.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 2201 OR your whole force is destroyed OR NOT (lose ≤1 of your own units)).
You have at most 26 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Three enemy squads hide in three different directions: NE, SE, and a non-obvious mid-north pocket. A naive east-only sweep finds only two before the clock runs out. Read where the unexplored mass is after each contact, then commit there. Discover three, two losses max, within about 32 turns.
WIN WHEN: spot ≥3 enemy units AND before game tick 2800 AND lose ≤2 of your own units.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 2801 OR your whole force is destroyed).
You have at most 32 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Four enemy squads: two obvious on the east-bound axes, one behind the spawn in the far-NW strip, one tucked in a tight south-of-mid pocket. Best-effort sweeps find two or three; only inferring from remaining fog mass gets all four. Two losses max, within about 39 turns.
WIN WHEN: spot ≥4 enemy units AND before game tick 3500 AND lose ≤2 of your own units.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 3501 OR your whole force is destroyed).
You have at most 40 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

title: Count the Threat — Commit a Force Sized EXACTLY to the Hidden Count

raw.realWorldMeaning: State estimation under partial observability where over-counting wastes resources and under-counting commits blind to a binding decision — you need the EXACT census, not an upper bound. The agent scouts the fog to count hidden enemy units, then commits a build of EXACTLY that many army units. Build too many → LOSS; build too few → LOSS; only a correctly-sized commit WINS.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Warehouse inventory pass before committing to a binding purchase order: probe enough shelves to satisfy the count, then commit the purchase at EXACTLY that quantity. Over-ordering wastes budget and shelf space; under-ordering breaks the downstream commit.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: ERQA state-estimation, POMDP exact-count sub-tasks, ScienceWorld inventory, ICU triage exact census, inventory-before-commit, BFCL strict parameter fidelity (count-exact)
raw.author: openra-bench

summary.en: State estimation under partial observability where over-counting wastes resources and under-counting commits blind to a binding decision — you need the EXACT census, not an upper bound. The agent scouts the fog to count hidden enemy units, then commits a build of EXACTLY that many army units. Build too many → LOSS; build too few → LOSS; only a correctly-sized commit WINS.
summary.zh: State estimation under partial observability where over-counting wastes resources and under-counting commits blind to a binding decision — you need the EXACT census, not an upper bound. The agent scouts the fog to count hidden enemy units, then commits a build of EXACTLY that many army units. Build too many → LOSS; build too few → LOSS; only a correctly-sized commit WINS.

en:
Three hidden enemy units sit clustered in a single fog pocket on the north-east half. Scout with the jeep until you have read the count, then build EXACTLY three rifle infantry (e1). Building a fourth busts the over-commit fail; stopping at two never reaches the build target. Within about 30 turns.
WIN WHEN: spot ≥3 enemy units AND have EXACTLY 3 'e1' (no more, no fewer) AND not before game tick 800 AND before game tick 2400.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 2401 OR have ≥4 'e1' OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 30 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Five hidden enemy UNITS are spread across two fog pockets on the north-east and south-east halves of the map. An enemy supply silo also sits between the clusters — it is a BUILDING, NOT a unit, and must NOT be counted toward the build target. Scout with both jeeps until you have read the unit count, then build EXACTLY five rifle infantry (e1). A sixth busts the over-commit fail; stopping at four or counting the silo into the build misses the spec. Within about 45 turns.
WIN WHEN: spot ≥5 enemy units AND have EXACTLY 5 'e1' (no more, no fewer) AND not before game tick 1500 AND before game tick 3600.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 3601 OR have ≥6 'e1' OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 45 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Five hidden enemy units are spread across both halves of the map under fog. Two enemy buildings (a silo and a turret) sit on the map but they are NOT units and must NOT be counted. The cluster arrangement rotates per seed — memorising "always scout north-east" misses two or three of the five on the south-heavy seed. Split the two jeeps across both lanes, read the count, build EXACTLY five rifle infantry. A sixth busts the over-commit fail; stopping at four misses the spec. Within about 45 turns.
WIN WHEN: spot ≥5 enemy units AND have EXACTLY 5 'e1' (no more, no fewer) AND not before game tick 1500 AND before game tick 3600.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 3601 OR have ≥6 'e1' OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 45 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

title: Read the Fog — Drive Scouts Into Every Unexplored Pocket

raw.realWorldMeaning: Path planning is solved; the hard part is reading an occupancy grid correctly to tell explored cells from the unknown frontier and pushing sensors into EACH unknown pocket instead of re-scanning known space or committing one blind heading.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: SLAM frontier detection — picking the next unexplored cell to drive a scout robot toward, for every disjoint frontier
raw.author: openra-bench

summary.en: Path planning is solved; the hard part is reading an occupancy grid correctly to tell explored cells from the unknown frontier and pushing sensors into EACH unknown pocket instead of re-scanning known space or committing one blind heading.
summary.zh: Path planning is solved; the hard part is reading an occupancy grid correctly to tell explored cells from the unknown frontier and pushing sensors into EACH unknown pocket instead of re-scanning known space or committing one blind heading.

en:
One hidden enemy marker sits far east, off the scouts' spawn rows, inside a single contiguous fog mass. The unknown IS the eastern dark band — drive a scout into it. Generous clock, but stalling or sticking near spawn never enters the pocket. Discover at least one enemy building within about 25 turns.
WIN WHEN: spot ≥1 enemy buildings AND before game tick 2200.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 2201 OR your whole force is destroyed).
You have at most 26 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

The frontier splits in two — a near pocket and a far one. Two hidden marker buildings must both be discovered. A decoy enemy squad sits inside the already-seen band to bait scouts into re-tread; the second marker is far NE and only a deliberate split push reveals it in time. Within about 32 turns.
WIN WHEN: spot ≥2 enemy buildings AND before game tick 2800.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 2801 OR your whole force is destroyed).
You have at most 32 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Three fog pockets at three corners — far NE, far SE, and a NW strip — each hiding one marker building. A decoy in the seen centre pulls scouts off the true frontier and your spawn corner varies by seed. Discover all three, within about 39 turns. Only a simultaneous read of all three fog pockets fits the clock.
WIN WHEN: spot ≥3 enemy buildings AND before game tick 3500.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 3501 OR your whole force is destroyed).
You have at most 40 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

title: Power Budget Online — Keep the Grid Positive While Expanding

raw.realWorldMeaning: Electrical-grid bring-up under a live capacity budget. The agent runs a base whose single Power Plant only just covers its standing load (+20 of headroom). The task is to EXPAND production — bring up an Ore Refinery, a War Factory, a Service Depot and an armour line — while keeping the grid in positive surplus the whole time. Each new powered load must have generation brought online AHEAD of it: build additional Power Plants and bring them up before the production buildings. A model that energises the refinery on the single starter plant drives the grid to negative surplus, the engine throttles every production queue to 50% speed, and the build-out overruns the deadline. A model that never builds power at all also misses the required gross-provided-power floor. Only an ongoing "generation ahead of demand" budget discipline wins.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Capacity planning for a commissioning operator energising a new industrial site: each powered subsystem (the processing line, the fabrication cell, the maintenance bay) must be matched by spare generation BEFORE it is switched on, or the substation browns out and every line on the bus runs slow. The operator must schedule generator capacity ahead of load growth — not power everything first, but bring generation online ahead of each new load — exactly the build-Power-Plant / build-production interleave this pack tests.

title: Procedural Checklist — No Deviation, No Skip, No Reorder

raw.realWorldMeaning: Follow an explicit ordered checklist with zero deviation: every named step must be performed in the exact prescribed order. The decision is literal ORDER compliance under a restricted action API — not where to go or how, but WHEN each step is performed relative to the others. Skipping a step, reordering steps, rushing straight to the final step, or idling all fail the procedure. The bench analogue of an aviation pre-flight checklist (where the order of checks is a flight-safety property, not a stylistic preference) and SOP compliance generally (no skip / no reorder).
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Procedural compliance: a robot must satisfy a named ordered checklist (visit checkpoint A, then B, then C, then D) within a cycle-time budget where step ORDER is graded, not just the end state — an out-of-order visit, a skipped step, or an idle all fail the procedure inspection.

title: Scout, Then Branch — Conditional IF/ELSE Procedure Execution

raw.realWorldMeaning: Conditional procedure execution: the operator is handed an explicit IF/ELSE runbook ("IF the enemy outpost is NORTH, attack NORTH; ELSE attack SOUTH") but does not know which antecedent is live. The capability under test is the read-then-dispatch loop — scout to OBSERVE the condition, BRANCH on what is seen, then EXECUTE the matching procedure. A fixed unconditional policy executes one branch on faith and is wrong on every seed where the other branch is correct.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Conditional tool-use / runbook branching under uncertainty: an incident-response agent follows a decision tree whose fork is gated on a sensor reading — symptom A dispatches procedure A, symptom B dispatches procedure B. Skipping the diagnostic step and committing to one procedure is correct half the time and a misfire the other half. The robust doctrine is observe-the-condition-then-branch, never branch-on-faith.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: τ²-bench conditional tool-use, IFBench conditional instruction, runbook branching
raw.author: openra-bench

en:

WIN WHEN: (in this exact order: spot ≥1 enemy buildings → THEN → destroy the enemy tent at the base near (20,4) AND own ≥1 'fact' building(s) AND before game tick 5400 OR in this exact order: spot ≥1 enemy buildings → THEN → destroy the enemy tent at the base near (20,36) AND own ≥1 'fact' building(s) AND before game tick 5400).
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 5401 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 66 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Same runbook — scout, then branch — but the enemy flank isn't given. Drive a jeep to discover the outpost, read whether it's NORTH or SOUTH, then send the four tanks to THAT flank and raze the barracks. Yard alive, within about 60 turns. Skipping the scout leaves the then-chain stuck at clause one.

title: Selective Action — Move the Jeeps, Do NOT Move the Tanks

raw.realWorldMeaning: Conditional standard-operating-procedure: the order has both a positive and a negative clause ("do X to units of class C; do NOT do anything to units of class D"). The operator's skill is to identify the targeted subset, act on it, and leave the rest untouched. Spraying the same action over the whole fleet is the classic failure mode — and is what the IFBench / BFCL V4 negative-instruction families measure.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Mixed-asset fleet with a per-class action allowlist for this mission: forklifts may move pallets; the autonomous floor scrubber must stay docked. The fleet controller must NOT issue a move command to the scrubber even if the scene is messy and the scrubber would naively be the "obvious next agent" to act.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: IFBench conditional / edge-case instruction, BFCL V4 negative instruction compliance, conditional SOP compliance, selective-action discipline
raw.author: openra-bench

WIN WHEN: get ≥3 'jeep' units into region (90,20) r=6 AND before game tick 4500.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 4501 OR your whole force is destroyed).
You have at most 55 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

title: ROE Recon — Reach the Observation Point Without Firing a Shot

title: Builder-Only Role — Build Under Visible Threat, No Combat Calls

raw.realWorldMeaning: Role-scoped operator must execute the build task without escalating into combat even when the threat is visible. The bench enforces an RBAC allowlist: build / place_building / move_units / stop / observe are permitted; any combat call (attack_unit, attack_move) is a procedure violation and instant LOSS. The point of the cell is separation-of-duties discipline under temptation — a passive (or slowly-encroaching) enemy is visible and chips the base, but reaching for an attack tool fails the run before any damage matters.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Provisioning robot forbidden from any actuator-level attack action. A construction agent scoped to deploy / place must complete the layout even when sensors report a nearby adversary; engaging the adversary is outside the role's capability surface and counts as a policy violation.

title: Defensive ROE — Hold the Base Using Stance and Positioning, Not Attack Orders

raw.realWorldMeaning: A defensive rules-of-engagement drill: the unit's brief is to hold a fixed asset (the base `fact`) against probing raiders, but the offensive tool (`attack_unit` / `attack_move`) is OFF-LIMITS. The only permitted commands are positional (`move_units`) and stance changes (`set_stance`) — the defenders auto-fire on intruders once their stance is lifted from HoldFire. A single forbidden attack order forfeits the mission. The skill is procedural: hold the role discipline (react only; do not pursue; do not initiate) even when the obvious local-solve is to call the attack tool.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: A security guard's standing orders. Fire only if engaged; do not pursue, do not initiate. The guard's role is positional plus stance-driven; the offensive command is off the allowlist even when an intruder is in view. The mission succeeds when the asset is intact and the intruders that walked into the defended footprint were neutralised by the stance-driven auto-fire — NOT by the guard issuing an attack order.

title: Strict Ordered Procedure — Place the Buildings in the Exact Mandated Sequence

raw.realWorldMeaning: Execute a procedure whose steps must run in a STRICT order: doing step 3 before step 2 invalidates the procedure, never recovers, and fails the run. The bench analogue of an aviation pre-flight checklist (skipping a step makes the next-step check meaningless) or a database migration where index-create-before-data-load is mandatory. The decision is literal ORDER compliance — not what or where, but WHEN relative to the other steps. A model that "eventually" placed every step in any order STILL fails: the procedure is graded on order, not on the final state.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: An assembly-line robot following a strict sequence (place rivet 1, then bracket, then rivet 2) where reversing a step destroys the earlier work — out-of-order assembly never recovers and fails inspection.

title: Strict Tool-Allowlist Fidelity — Transit the Jeeps Using Only Allowed Tools

raw.realWorldMeaning: Clean BFCL-style tool-allowlist fidelity. The agent is briefed with an explicit allowlist [move_units, build, place_building, observe, stop] and an explicit forbidden list [attack_unit, attack_move, set_stance, harvest, repair, sell, set_rally_point]. The mission is satisfiable with only `move_units` (transit four jeeps to an egress region while the pre-placed `fact` stays intact). One invocation of any forbidden tool fails the run immediately. No enemy combatants are placed along the corridor; the discipline must hold under quiet conditions, not under distractor pressure. The *-under-pressure sibling adds a patrol-as-temptation; this pack is the quiet baseline.

title: Cluttered Tool Surface — Ignore the Distractor Tools and Just Move

raw.realWorldMeaning: The agent receives a CLUTTERED toolset (9 tools) where only TWO are on the critical path for the current task (move + observe). The other seven are MAXIMALLY SALIENT distractors: a visible weak enemy invites `attack_unit`; cash on hand and a pre-placed base invite `build` / `place_building`; `harvest` / `set_rally_ point` / `set_stance` / `attack_move` look generally useful but do nothing for THIS goal. The discipline is to recognise which subset of a large API is actually relevant and ignore the rest — every off-path tool call either interrupts the unit's move order, lures units into a costly engagement, or burns the model's turn budget while the within_ticks clock keeps ticking.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: A teleoperation panel with dozens of buttons (manipulator, nav, gripper, vision, comms, logging…) but only two are on the critical path for THIS mission. A disciplined operator runs the two-button procedure; a junior operator who reaches for every salient button wastes the window or causes collateral damage. The skill is API/relevance discrimination under no explicit "don't touch X" instruction.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: τ²-bench multi-distractor handling, BFCL V4 cluttered-API relevance, IFBench distraction resistance, junior-operator discipline test
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Distractor Tool Discipline — Ignore the Tempting Irrelevant Build Palette

raw.realWorldMeaning: Tool-palette discipline under distraction. The operator has a large API surface — movement, attack, build, place_building, observe — but only ONE of those tools is needed to complete the mission. The remaining tools are visible, available, and tempting (the build palette in particular looks like "real work" and feels productive), but they are irrelevant to the win and spending turns on them runs out the deadline. Unlike a strict allowlist scenario (where forbidden tools trip a violation counter and the bench grades you on rule-following), this cell has NO forbidden tools — the test is whether the agent REASONS about which tools are RELEVANT to the task and ignores the others, the way a senior operator ignores the eighteen flags `kubectl apply` exposes and uses only the two they actually need.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Mobile robot with a rich actuator palette (manipulator, weld, cut, drill, inspect, navigate) is assigned a pure navigate-to-waypoint mission. The other actuators are available and many of them produce visible feedback if invoked, but invoking them wastes the energy / time budget. The disciplined policy ignores the irrelevant actuators and just navigates; the kitchen-sink policy exhausts itself running every actuator it can see.

title: Commit Under Uncertainty — Pick the One Region That Hides the Survivor

raw.realWorldMeaning: Path planning to any point is solved. The unsolved problem is deciding which of several unexplored regions to commit a time/fuel-limited searcher to when only one hides the target and going to the wrong one first means you never reach the right one in time. That commitment-under-uncertainty step is the real search-and-rescue problem, not the navigation.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: UAV/UGV search-and-rescue frontier selection: with limited endurance and several candidate search cells, choose the cell most likely to contain the survivor before the battery dies.
raw.author: berta

title: Safe vs Fast — Choose the Survivable Longer Route Over the Deadly Shortcut

raw.realWorldMeaning: Shortest-path is solved. The unsolved decision is whether the shortest path is the right path: a direct corridor may pass through a hazard that destroys the vehicle, while a longer perimeter route completes the mission intact. Choosing the survivable plan over the fastest one, given a deadline that the detour still satisfies, is the actual mission-planning problem.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Field-robot route selection under hazard: a delivery/inspection robot must reject the shortest path when it crosses a no-go hazard zone and instead commit to a longer but survivable route that still meets the time window.
raw.author: berta

summary.en: Shortest-path is solved. The unsolved decision is whether the shortest path is the right path: a direct corridor may pass through a hazard that destroys the vehicle, while a longer perimeter route completes the mission intact. Choosing the survivable plan over the fastest one, given a deadline that the detour still satisfies, is the actual mission-planning problem.

YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 2701 OR NOT (lose ≤0 of your own units) OR your whole force is destroyed).
You have at most 32 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

title: Blockade Bypass — Reach the Objective by the Survivable Detour

raw.realWorldMeaning: Route-risk assessment with a visibly hard direct path and a longer survivable alternative under a binding attrition cap. The cap punishes brute force; the clock punishes infinite detour. The decision is committing the force to the route that actually makes the deadline alive.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Field-robot mission routing rejecting a hazardous shortest path for a survivable longer one within a time window — but the longer path is not free, so the model must weigh attrition vs deadline rather than always preferring the safe option.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: MicroRTS route-risk / hazardous-corridor sub-tasks, PlanBench cost-vs-survival route planning, field-robotics: contested vs detour route under SLA, convoy routing with attrition budget
raw.author: yiyu-tian

en:
Reach the objective region near (110,20) within about 39 turns, losing no more than four units. A heavy central garrison (around (46..57, 20..22)) out-trades you badly — pushing or even probing it bleeds past the cap before you arrive. The northern detour past a light picket at (55,5) costs ~600 extra ticks but only ~one unit. Pick the survivable route.
WIN WHEN: get a unit into region (110,20) r=6 AND before game tick 3500 AND lose ≤4 of your own units.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 3501 OR your whole force is destroyed OR NOT (lose ≤4 of your own units)).
You have at most 40 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Same map, tighter cap (≤2 losses) and a 2800-tick deadline. The corridor route is now infeasible — the heavy garrison guarantees you blow the cap. The northern detour is the only path with positive margin, but commit immediately; dithering near the corridor before bouncing burns ticks. Within about 32 turns.
WIN WHEN: get a unit into region (110,20) r=6 AND before game tick 2800 AND lose ≤2 of your own units.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 2801 OR your whole force is destroyed OR NOT (lose ≤2 of your own units)).
You have at most 32 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

WIN WHEN: get a unit into region (110,20) r=6 AND before game tick 2400 AND lose ≤1 of your own units.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 2401 OR your whole force is destroyed OR NOT (lose ≤1 of your own units)).
You have at most 28 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

title: Recover From Cash Depletion — Rebuild Refinery After Mid-Episode Strike

raw.realWorldMeaning: Financial recovery after a sudden cash drain caused by an emergency outflow that destroys the operation's income channel. The agent inherits a normal operating economy with just enough reserve cash for ONE refinery rebuild; an exogenous strike destroys the refinery mid-episode; income halts. The agent must notice the loss, commit the indivisible reserve to rebuilding the refinery, and redirect the harvester back to the patch — fast enough that the revenue bar is still cleared before the deadline. Stalling, ignoring the destruction, or spending the reserve on army units all miss the bar.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Post-disaster operations restart after the critical processing node is destroyed by an external event mid-mission. The autonomous operator has one collector still alive, no working capital beyond a single processing-node rebuild allowance, and a deadline. Recovery requires identifying the lost asset, committing the reserve to rebuilding it (not to defenders or expansion), and re-tasking the collector back to the source once the new node is operational.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: financial cash-crisis recovery, SC2 cash-drain rebuild, DR after critical-infra loss, bankruptcy turnaround under deadline
raw.author: openra-bench-wave-6

en:
You start with a yard, power, refinery, one harvester, two near patches, two heavy-tank defenders, and $1400. A lone enemy heavy tank is staged beside the refinery — your defenders intercept and the refinery survives. Just commit the harvester to a patch cell and start the harvest cycle. Economy value 2500, refinery and yard alive, within about 70 turns.
WIN WHEN: reach economy value ≥2500 (cash+ore) AND own ≥1 'proc' building(s) AND own ≥1 'fact' building(s) AND before game tick 6300.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 6301 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 70 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Same base and $1400 reserve, but TWO enemy heavies attack the refinery and overwhelm the defenders — the refinery falls around tick 270 and the harvest loop dies. Queue another refinery (cost $1400 — the reserve covers it exactly), place it beside the yard, then re-issue harvest on the surviving worker. Economy value 2500, refinery and yard alive, within about 70 turns.
WIN WHEN: reach economy value ≥2500 (cash+ore) AND own ≥1 'proc' building(s) AND own ≥1 'fact' building(s) AND before game tick 6300.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 6301 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 70 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

Same recovery, harder: FOUR heavy tanks raze both the refinery AND a barracks early (tent down ~tick 180, refinery ~tick 270). Reserve is still $1400 — exactly one refinery. Rebuild the refinery first (the barracks isn't on the win predicate), re-issue harvest. Economy value 2500, refinery and yard alive, within about 70 turns.
WIN WHEN: reach economy value ≥2500 (cash+ore) AND own ≥1 'proc' building(s) AND own ≥1 'fact' building(s) AND before game tick 6300.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 6301 OR NOT (own ≥1 'fact' building(s))).
You have at most 70 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

title: Deadline Shortened Midway — Crash the Schedule When the Budget Shrinks

raw.realWorldMeaning: A plan was paced against one deadline; mid-execution the deadline is pulled FORWARD. A team still working to the original date misses entirely — the only recovery is to compress the schedule: drop every slack activity, commit all resources at once, and accelerate. The intended policy does not pace leisurely against a generous nominal budget; it executes fast from the start (or instantly re-paces the moment the budget shrinks), so a mid-episode deadline cut still finds the objective achievable. A leisurely pace that would have met the original deadline now loses.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Real-time task re-planning under a tightened time budget: a delivery robot routed for a 30-minute window is told mid-route the package is now needed in 12 — it must drop optional sub-goals and take the fastest path immediately, not finish the leisurely plan. Likewise a manufacturing line told a shipment moved up must crash its schedule (parallelise, cut slack) rather than run the original cadence.

title: Compound Incident — Multi-Front Simultaneous Pressure (Defence + Economy + Tech)

raw.realWorldMeaning: Ops triage during a compound incident — three independent failures must be handled simultaneously, none of which can be sequenced or paused. Your base is under a hunt charge (defence), the harvesters feeding income are being raided (economy), and a tech objective (war factory) must be completed before a hard deadline. Focusing on any single pressure forfeits the others; the intended play keeps all three loops running in parallel, funding the tech with the harvest income that the defenders are simultaneously protecting.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Disaster-recovery multi-system failure — a control room handles a security event (perimeter under attack), a throughput event (data pipeline workers under harassment), and a planned upgrade (capability rollout) at the same time. Pausing the upgrade to fight the security incident misses the rollout SLA; abandoning the pipeline to harden the perimeter starves the upgrade of resources. The capability under test is parallel-task triage under genuine simultaneous pressure.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2 multi-front simultaneous pressure, ops triage during compound incident, DR multi-system failure, military theater-wide simultaneous threats
raw.author: openra-bench

en:

WIN WHEN: own a 'weap' AND own a 'proc' AND have ≥1 'harv' AND own a 'fact' AND reach economy value ≥1000 (cash+ore) AND before game tick 5400.
YOU LOSE IF: (not before game tick 5401 OR NOT (own a 'fact') OR NOT (have ≥1 'harv')).
You have at most 61 decision turns; acting decisively and early matters.

title: Objective Change Midway — Pivot When the Goal Shifts

raw.realWorldMeaning: The mission objective changes mid-episode. Phase 1 is an early goal — stage the force at a forward region; once that is achieved a DIFFERENT phase-2 goal is revealed — raze the enemy construction yard at a far region. The agent must pursue the early goal first and only then pivot to the new one. A policy that commits to the phase-2 goal from the start fails phase 1 (the ordered chain never latches its first clause); a policy that only completes phase 1 and stops fails phase 2. The win is the ordered `then` chain over both goals AND a deadline — only a genuine goal-conditional pivot satisfies it.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Goal-conditional task execution with a mid-task re-spec: a mobile robot is dispatched to reach a staging waypoint; on arrival the operator updates the task — now also clear a target at a second, further site. The robot must complete the original navigation goal first and then re-condition its policy on the new goal, finishing the revised task inside the same energy budget rather than either ignoring the update or abandoning the first leg.

raw.author: openra-bench

title: Objective Shift with OR-Clause — Pivot to the Feasible Path

raw.realWorldMeaning: Two acceptable objectives are on the table; mid-episode it becomes clear the originally-natural one is infeasible inside the budget; the agent must abandon that path and re-target the second (still-acceptable) objective without exhausting its means. The win is the `any_of` over the two paths AND a hard attrition cap AND a deadline — a brute-force commit to the heavy path overruns the cap; stalling overruns the deadline; only the recognise-and-pivot policy converges inside both teeth.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Mid-mission objective change: a robotic survey platform sent to sample Site A finds Site A inaccessible (unexpected obstacle / hazard exceeds the platform's risk envelope); the science plan accepted EITHER Site A or Site B as the day's sample, so the platform must re-plan to Site B inside the same energy / daylight budget instead of returning empty-handed.

title: Graceful Degradation — Press On After a Non-Critical Base Loss

raw.realWorldMeaning: Triage an exogenous partial loss. Mid-mission, a scripted strike razes a NON-CRITICAL slice of the agent's base — an outer pillbox and one of two harvesters — while the war-critical core (construction yard, refinery, power, war factory, service depot) is untouched. The intended policy performs battle-damage assessment: it recognises the lost assets are NOT on the win path and PRESSES ON with the core objective — field the heavy-armour establishment UP to the required strength and clear the eastern garrison defending the enemy construction yard — rather than diverting its decision turns to panic-rebuilding the non-essentials. Rebuilding the razed pillbox + harvester burns the turns the agent needed to commission the war-critical tanks; the establishment and kill bars then go unmet.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Graceful degradation under partial subsystem loss. A field robot loses a non-mission-essential sensor or a spare battery pack mid-task; a brittle controller halts the primary task to restore the lost component, blowing the mission deadline, while a robust one assesses that the loss does not block the objective and continues. The discrimination is incident triage — distinguishing a critical failure (which DOES require a stop-and-fix) from a cosmetic / redundant one (which must be ignored so the main effort stays on schedule).
raw.benchmarkAnchor: graceful degradation, incident triage, critical-vs-noncritical assessment, PlanBench replanning under exogenous loss, military battle-damage assessment

title: Surprise Second Wave — Reserve Forces for the Follow-On

raw.realWorldMeaning: Adversarial robustness on the temporal axis: the obvious threat (a 4-unit cluster near the agent's starting vision) is just the OPENING; a SECOND wave was pre-placed at a fog corner and closes in from an unexpected bearing by ~tick 1500 in a hunt pattern. Winning requires destroying BOTH waves AND keeping the base AND keeping enough force alive. The relevant capability is RESERVING capacity for a follow-on attack — not committing every defender to the visible battle and chasing routers far from the base. "Battle finished, push deep" is the canonical military / SRE failure mode this trains against.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Incident-after-incident triage: a fresh page arrives from a different subsystem the moment the operator resolves the visible incident; the operator must keep enough on-call capacity in reserve to handle the follow-on instead of fully committing every responder to the first symptom. Adversarial robustness: treating the first observable threat as ground truth and over-fitting the response to it leaves the system exposed when the adversary stages a second engagement from a different angle.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: adversarial robustness: surprise wave handling, military follow-on wave doctrine, ops: incident-after-incident triage, SC2 second-attack timing
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Force-Regen After Attrition — Rebuild Combat Force Mid-Episode

raw.realWorldMeaning: Reactive replan to bring a force up to establishment. An ongoing offensive operation begins UNDER-STRENGTH — the standing column is below the force structure the mission requires; the agent has reserve cash to commission the missing units from the war factory; the offensive deadline is real. The model must notice the gap (units_summary shows fewer combat tanks than the required establishment), commit the reserve to building the combat type (not to a different unit or to nothing), AND continue the original mission (clear the eastern garrison defending the enemy construction yard) fast enough that the deadline still bites.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Military force-regen / SC2 rebuild-after-trade. A theater operation is fielded below establishment and must build up to strength from the rear-area production base mid-mission; the supervisor has a discrete replacement budget; the operational objective and timeline are fixed. The discrimination is whether the model recognises the gap in the advertised force structure AND issues the production order in time to keep the offensive on schedule; ignoring the gap (assaulting with the reduced force) under-strengths the assault and busts the establishment bar; spending the budget on the wrong unit type breaks the offensive composition; doing nothing busts the deadline.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: PlanBench replanning under exogenous loss, ScienceWorld error recovery, military force-regen / unit replacement, SC2 rebuild-after-trade
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Search & Destroy - Sweep a Scattered Enemy Off the Arena

raw.realWorldMeaning: A wide arena hides a chain of separate enemy squads, scattered in a zigzag across the whole map and in fog. The task is to SWEEP the arena - spread a small armoured team across the off-axis groups, reveal and destroy enough of them before the clock runs out, without losing the team. The skill is coordinated coverage of unknown space (spread out, scout, converge), not single-unit micro or a one-spot auto-brawl. This is the find-the-enemy counterpart to the close-range 1v1 duel.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Multi-robot search-and-destroy: sweep and clear a bounded area with several dispersed targets within a time budget, keeping the team intact.
raw.author: ported-from-training

title: Scout and Report — Reveal the Far Target, Then Extract the Team

raw.realWorldMeaning: Military intelligence reconnaissance with mandatory full-team recovery. The scout team must surface a specific FAR enemy installation AND bring the entire team back INTACT for the intelligence to be delivered. Real intel-and-extract doctrine treats neither bare discovery NOR a partial-team return as a success — the channel is the report (requires return) AND the asset is the team (requires zero losses). The pack tests whether the agent treats "saw the target" or "one jeep made it home" as success rather than the binding "discovered AND full team extracted" criterion.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Multi-drone reconnaissance overflight with return-to-base + zero-attrition acceptance: the mission counts as a success only if the platforms reveal the named target AND ALL platforms recover. A one-way commit that surfaces the target but loses any drone is a partial failure, not a win — the report channel requires both the data AND the platforms back at base for the next mission.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: military intelligence reconnaissance (recon-and-extract), SC2 scout-and-return for info, drone surveillance with return-to-base, intel ops: gather then withdraw
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Scout and Survive — Reveal the Objective, Then Return Alive

raw.realWorldMeaning: Reconnaissance with mandatory recovery. The scout is both the sensor and the worker — losing it costs the info channel and the asset. Real scout doctrine never treats discovery as the terminal goal; the scout must come back so the information is delivered AND the unit is preserved for the next mission. The pack tests whether the agent treats "saw the objective" or "scout returned home alive" as the success criterion.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: UAV/UGV reconnaissance with return-to-base endurance: the mission succeeds only if the platform reveals the target AND lands safely. A one-way commit that surfaces the target but ditches the platform is a partial failure, not a win.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2 worker-scout micro (scout must survive), ERQA partial-observability under preservation, military UAV reconnaissance with return-to-base, intelligence-gather-and-extract missions

title: Scout Count Defenders — Build Force EXACTLY Matched to Counted Threat

raw.realWorldMeaning: Exact-count perception coupled to a binding force-sizing decision. The agent must drive a scout into the fog to read EXACTLY how many enemy defenders are at the objective, then commission an attack force sized to defeat THAT count — no more (over-build wastes the production queue past the deadline), no less (under-build loses the attrition trade). The capability under test is COUNT-AWARE PRODUCTION SIZING, not bare scouting and not bare construction.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Inventory-driven dispatch under a binding deadline: an autonomous fleet manager must observe how many obstacles block a corridor before allocating the right number of clearing robots — sending too few robots fails the corridor opening, sending the whole fleet wastes the dispatch window on already-cleared sectors. The advertised capability is count-then-allocate, not over-allocate-to-be-safe.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: POMDP exact-count, ScienceWorld census, SC2 scout-count
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Scout Cycle — Keep Information Fresh as the Battlefield Changes

raw.realWorldMeaning: Observation is not a one-shot. The agent scouts the battlefield, sees the visible enemy force, and commits a plan; mid-engagement, the battlefield changes (reinforcements arrive, the enemy maneuvers behind fog) and a stale picture is wrong. The intended policy CYCLES the scout — keeps pushing perception probes back into the previously-observed area to detect the change before the plan is invalidated. This is the perception cell that uniquely tests information FRESHNESS, not just initial reading.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Continuous SLAM / re-localisation: a robot that maps the room once and then drives by dead-reckoning crashes the instant a chair moves. A re-perceiving robot loops the lidar back across seen-but-stale regions. Similarly, an autonomous-vehicle perception stack cannot rely on a single frame — it must continually re-observe to detect lane changes, new pedestrians, and obstacles that appeared since the last glance.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2 information refresh (scout cycling for army-position updates), continuous-SLAM re-localisation under environmental change, autonomous-vehicle perception (per-frame re-detection of dynamic obstacles), wargame intelligence cycle — collection → analysis → re-collection
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Counter-Recon — Deny Enemy Vision: Kill the Scouts Before They Report

raw.realWorldMeaning: An enemy scout has taken up an observation post overlooking your base; left alone it completes its report and the enemy gains a full picture of your disposition. The agent must locate and DESTROY every enemy scout before the report window closes. Sitting still lets the report complete; covering only ONE recon vector leaves the other scout's report intact. The pack tests counter-reconnaissance: actively denying the adversary vision by hunting down EVERY scout, not merely defending one approach.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Counter-surveillance / intrusion prevention: an adversary's reconnaissance probes are mapping the defended site, and each probe exfiltrates its findings once it has observed long enough. The defender must detect and neutralise EVERY probe before its report window elapses — a passive posture that merely watches the probes loses the information war, and neutralising one probe while ignoring another still leaks the map.

raw.author: openra-bench

title: Scout the Two Corners — Find the Enemy Base Direction Before Striking

raw.realWorldMeaning: Direction-of-target perception with two candidate locations and a finite reconnaissance budget. The enemy base could be at ONE OF TWO far corners; the agent must dispatch scouts to confirm each candidate, then commit the main strike force to the correct corner. Picking a corner blind half-wins and half-busts the clock on the round trip; only the deliberate scout-both-then-commit play converges every time. The capability under test is the model's discipline to PERFORM AND READ the perception step before committing the main resource.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: Military intelligence triage: a battalion commander has two reported enemy locations and a small reconnaissance asset; the commander dispatches scouts to BOTH candidate sites, identifies which holds the actionable target, and commits the main force only after the intel is back. Pre-committing the main force without the scout trip strikes the wrong site half the time and burns the operational window. The doctrine under test is scout-then-strike, not commit-on-faith.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: ERQA direction-reading, military intelligence triage, SC2 scout direction
raw.author: openra-bench

title: Early Warning — Scout to Detect the Incoming Army Axis, Then Intercept

raw.realWorldMeaning: Early-warning intrusion detection paired with a targeted response. An enemy force is inbound and the agent's defenders are at the base, but the agent does NOT know which axis the army will arrive on. Pure defence-without-scouting cannot pre-position the defenders correctly; pure offence-without-scouting commits the defenders to the wrong lane; only a deliberate scout step — push sensors out, READ the approach axis, then re-position the defenders FORWARD on the correct lane — wins. This is the perception decision that precedes a targeted defensive commitment.
raw.roboticsAnalogue: NORAD-style early-warning network paired with QRF dispatch: sparse perimeter sensors LOCALISE an incoming threat; the response force is then vectored to the localised lane, not spread across the whole perimeter. An IDS that detects the breach lane lets the SecOps response target the right subnet instead of fortifying every host. A reconnaissance-in-force screen detects the enemy axis of advance so the main body deploys on the correct lane.
raw.benchmarkAnchor: SC2 early-warn scout / scout-for-attack, NORAD-style early-warning systems, intrusion detection systems (IDS), military reconnaissance-in-force detection
raw.author: openra-bench
